card: Updates the p2p_eviction functional test to ensure it actually exercises block-time protection logic during peer eviction. Currently, the test connects block-sending peers first, allowing fallback connection-time protection to shield them from eviction even if block-time protection is disabled. Connecting the block-sending peers last ensures that the test fails if block-time eviction protection regresses. No external dependencies exist.
evidence: PR description demonstrates the test currently passes even if the block transmission line is removed: 'This can be shown by deleting the line where the peers send their block (L71 on master): block_peer.send_blocks_and_test([block], node, success=True)'
Commit message notes that connecting peers last ensures the test fails if CompareNodeBlockTime protection in SelectNodeToEvict is removed.
problem: The functional test for node eviction passes even if block-time protection is broken or omitted entirely. Because the test currently connects block-sending peers first, fallback eviction logic protects the oldest peers by connection time, masking any defect in block-time eviction protection.

risk.why: Only modifies a Python functional test script, so any error would only cause test suite failures.

scope_notes: Small functional test fix in p2p_eviction.py.
summary: Fixes a false positive in test/functional/p2p_eviction.py by connecting block-sending inbound peers last instead of first. This ensures that the test specifically exercises eviction protection for nodes that recently provided novel blocks rather than falling back to protecting them based on connection age.
